maya: quick update from the FP8+AWQ/GPTQ smoke runs on h100/l40s
maya: ran conversion pipeline on gpt-j-6b variant with both GPTQ (4-bit) and AWQ (4-bit int-like) then enabled fp8 kernels on H100 and L40S
maya: immediate oddity: AWQ quantized model produces ~3.2% rouge delta vs fp32 baseline on long-context evals, GPTQ is ~1.1% 
ricardo: is the 3.2% consistent across seeds or only specific prompts?
sophia: saw similar delta locally, seems concentrated on prefix-heavy prompts (doc summarization)
maya: yes, prefix-heavy and chat-history builds. Short queries are fine. suspect kv-cache tiling vs scale folding interactions with AWQ per-channel scales
ben: any NaNs/crashes on H100?
maya: no hard crashes, but H100 FP8 kernel returned a couple of malformed logits (inf) in one run, automatically fell back to FP16 for that batch
taylor: L40S behaved more stable but had slightly higher latency when fallback triggered
ricardo: did you run with the quantization-compat shim we landed last week? could be handshake mismatch
maya: used the shim version from canary-2026-03-19, with the new scale-alias table enabled
sophia: logs: ```
[2026-03-19T21:12:04Z] kv_cache_tiler: tile_size=256 seq=4096
[2026-03-19T21:12:04Z] awq_convert: per_channel_scale_min=1.12e-3
[2026-03-19T21:12:04Z] kernel_fp8_exec: warning: activation_clamp overflow -> fallback(fp16)
```
maya: repro command I used: `./tools/quant_bakeoff --model gpt-j-6b --algo awq --backend h100 --enable-fp8-kernels --eval longdoc`
ben: can you paste the exact AWQ config? we need to know rounding mode and outlier clipping
maya: config: `awq_clip=0.02,awq_round=stochastic,per_channel=true,merge_bias=true`
sophia: small experiment: switched awq_round=nearest and delta dropped to ~1.8% but still worse than GPTQ
ricardo: interesting — rounding mode affecting long-context quality suggests subtle accumulation error across KV copies
taylor: I wonder if our prefix cache reuse multiplies quantization error when tiles straddle cache boundaries
maya: hypothesis: when tile boundaries align with cache checkpoints we get consistent scale alignment; misaligned tiles cause local rescaling and non-deterministic rounding -> quality drift
ben: can we try: 1) force tile_size=512, 2) disable merge_bias, 3) run deterministic rounding and compare
maya: queued those runs now, will post summary in ~45m
sophia: also: try a small patch that forces scale smoothing across layers: `scale = 0.9*prev_scale + 0.1*curr_scale` — saw improvement in a toy model
maya: opened a short PR with the smoothing patch and a smoke test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-infer/pull/4123
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for branch fp8-awq-smoke in staging at 2026-03-19T22:10:00Z
maya: note for oncall: this is non-blocking, only impacts canary evals. not rolling to prod yet :thumbsup:
ricardo: if smoothing helps, we should add opt-in knob, not default; need perf check
ben: also measure token-level perplexity drift, rouge alone might hide hallucination patterns
maya: will add per-token logp diffs and hallucination checks to the bakeoff harness
taylor: thanks — if we can reproduce deterministically we can bisect to a specific kernel kernel_version/commit
maya: attaching initial numbers in a gist: https://gist.github.com/maya-fp8/awq-smoke-1977702468
sophia: great, ping me when the tile_size runs finish, I can run the same on L40S infra
maya: will do. thanks all :pray:
